Detail

Chicago Cubs @ Washington Nationals, 3:45p

Summary

Both teams enter this one with something to prove, and a rookie lefty getting thrown to the wolves against a red-hot Cubs lineup adds some intrigue to an otherwise unremarkable pitching matchup. Chicago has been one of the better stories in baseball lately, riding an 8-2 stretch over their last ten games while sitting comfortably in wild-card position, and both the Cubs' offense (elite fielding and baserunning) and the Nationals' surprisingly potent attack (led by CJ Abrams' power) fuel strong tNERD marks near the top of today's slate. The real hook is Jackson Kent's debut: the Nationals' top lefty prospect posted a 2.35 ERA at Double-A before his strikeout rate dropped and walk rate climbed after a promotion to Triple-A. He'll face a Cubs team that reportedly mashes left-handed pitching, which is either a brutal welcome to the majors or a chance for early heroics. David Peterson, by contrast, is a solid-not-spectacular presence — his 4.84 pNERD is middling, buoyed mostly by some bad luck that suggests better results ahead. With a 14.70 gNERD, this game ranks near the top of today's games and comfortably above the historical average, thanks far more to lineups and stakes than to frontline arms.

Milwaukee Brewers @ San Diego Padres, 1:10p

Summary

This one's got playoff stakes and quietly excellent pitcher and team profiles, even if the two starters' NERD scores tell very different stories. The Padres, clinging to the fringes of the NL wild-card race, are hosting the sport's best record-holders in Milwaukee, and both clubs bring loaded bullpens and above-average NERD marks to the table—Milwaukee's 9.61 and San Diego's 9.84 are both comfortably above the historical mean, and their combined 13.04 gNERD sits well above today's 10.35 average. On the mound, Dustin May, a deadline pickup from St. Louis, brings mid-90s heat and a tidy xFIP-, though his road numbers this year have been rough. Robbie Ray, San Diego's own deadline addition from the Giants, has had an uneven Padres debut but reportedly settled into better form since, though his NERD score (0.97) reflects underlying command issues with elevated walk rates. May faced the Padres twice already this year as a Cardinal, adding a little familiarity to the mix. Watch for the bullpens and lineups to carry this one more than the arms.

Philadelphia Phillies @ St. Louis Cardinals, 11:15a

Summary

Wheeler and Leahy take the mound in a series rubber match with real playoff stakes attached — this one's worth your afternoon. The Phillies are clinging to a National League Wild Card spot, and Wheeler has been the engine of their second-half surge; Zack Wheeler has been on a bit of a roller coaster since the All-Star break, and he'll take the ball with a chance to stabilize things as the Phillies continue to fight for a National League Wild Card spot. His pNERD of 9.01 — well above today's field average of 4.66 — is built on elite whiff and contact-suppression skills; his xFIP- and swinging-strike rates both grade out as some of the best marks on the slate. Across town, Leahy isn't just a fifth-starter innings-eater anymore: St. Louis counters with Kyle Leahy, who has quietly rounded into form, carrying a 3.45 ERA and a 1.34 WHIP, striking out 21 percent while walking seven and a half percent. In his past four starts Leahy has posted a 2.35 ERA with a 1.08 WHIP, numbers that have quietly made this a legitimate pitching duel rather than a mismatch. Both offenses rank near the bottom of the league in production, so don't expect fireworks — this is a game to watch for pitching craft, not crooked scoreboards. The gNERD of 12.54 sits comfortably above the historical average (10.11) and today's average (10.35), making it one of the better-graded games on the board.

Seattle Mariners @ New York Yankees, 4:05p

Summary

Good, the losing streak angle is solid. Let me write the summary now.

A rebuilding Mariners team riding a five-game skid rolls into the Bronx, and while the underlying pitching matchup has some juice, don't expect fireworks from the lineups. Seattle has scored just five runs across that five-game losing streak and nine over its last seven, while the Yankees' offense is also cold with its top power bats banged up. The pitching, though, is the story: Bryce Miller brings a 7.19 pNERD built on a stingy xFIP-, elite strike rate, and mid-90s heat, and reporting on his split-finger's 28.5% whiff rate and a walk rate that borders on absurd — a 0.95 WHIP and just 15 free passes in 79 innings — explains why he's tough to work an inning against. Will Warren counters with a solid 5.47 pNERD, helped by a bit of positive luck suggesting his 4.18 ERA overstates how hittable he's actually been. Yankees' tNERD (8.07) dwarfs Seattle's anemic 2.82, driven by New York's barrel rate and clean glovework against a Mariners defense that's been a genuine liability. At 11.78, the gNERD lands solidly above average for today's slate — worth catching for the pitching duel, if not the lineups.

Pittsburgh Pirates @ Miami Marlins, 3:40p

Summary

Pittsburgh's in a rut and Miami's quietly building the more entertaining roster, but this game leans on two mid-tier arms rather than star power to make its case. The Pirates have lost six of their last seven games, and the malaise runs deeper than the standings — even ace Paul Skenes got a quick hook in a 2-0 shutout loss the night before this one, part of a stretch that's included four shutouts since the All-Star break. Carmen Mlodzinski takes the ball for Pittsburgh with modest scores across the board, but he pairs a low home-run rate with a nasty splitter that generates a strong whiff rate, giving him a real edge over Miami's Janson Junk, who's been homer-prone and comes with the lower pNERD of the two. Neither pitcher grades out as a marquee arm, but Junk's tendency to work deep counts and issue traffic keeps things unpredictable. The Marlins are the more interesting team on paper, with a tNERD comfortably above both the historic and today's averages, buoyed by strong baserunning, a young, inexpensive roster, and some positive regression-suggesting luck. With Pittsburgh missing O'Hearn, Cruz, and Keller to injury, Miami's lineup depth gives this one a slight watchability edge, but it's a solidly middle-of-the-pack game rather than a must-see.

Tampa Bay Rays @ Athletics, 12:05p

Summary

I have plenty to work with. Let me write the summary now.

Watch this one for Drew Rasmussen dominating a punchless Oakland lineup, not for any real drama—the A's are in freefall and the Rays are rolling. Rasmussen brings a tidy 8.48 pNERD into West Sacramento, backed by an xFIP- of 75 and mid-90s velocity, and he's coming off a start for Tampa Bay's finale after leading the Rays' pitching staff with a 2.75 ERA, making it no easy task for the A's bats to inflict damage. Jack Perkins counters with a respectable 6.39 pNERD on the stuff metrics, but the results haven't matched—he enters at 2-8 with a 7.04 ERA and 1.45 WHIP, and his outsized "luck" score suggests some regression relief may be overdue, though not enough to save this Oakland club. The Rays (5.68 tNERD) are hot, having just blown out the A's 12-4 behind a two-run blast from Junior Caminero, his 35th homer, tying him for the league lead, while the Athletics (2.22 tNERD) are mired in a seven-game home skid and missing key bats like Brent Rooker and Shea Langeliers to injury. At 11.39, the gNERD sits a bit above average—worth a look for the pitching matchup, not the drama.

Boston Red Sox @ Toronto Blue Jays, 4:07p

Summary

Not a marquee matchup, but there's a decent floor here thanks to two solid arms and a Blue Jays team that's underperforming its own talent. Boston limps into Toronto on a four-game losing streak, though the underlying numbers - Boston rolls into Rogers Centre on a four-game losing streak, but the underlying numbers over the last 10 games tell a different story: a .276 team average and a plus-26 run differential - suggest the Sox are better than their recent record. Suarez has been battling through short outings since returning from the IL, laboring through three innings against the White Sox last week and hasn't quite bounced back, limited to 4.0 and 4.2 innings in recent starts, though his xFIP still grades out strong. Soriano brings mid-90s velocity and a knuckle-curve that generates a 43.3% whiff rate that can shut down stretches of any lineup, and his pNERD actually edges Suarez's here. Toronto's offense is the drag on this one - bottom-of-the-barrel exit velocity and baserunning - but a plus fielding unit and bullpen give it just enough juice to keep this from being a total snooze. A middling-to-decent watch, elevated mostly by the pitching.

Cincinnati Reds @ Chicago White Sox, 4:40p

Summary

I have enough to write a solid summary now.

A middling pitching matchup between two clubs going nowhere fast, but the series opener already proved these teams can produce chaos. Cincinnati stole game one of this set in extra innings after trailing by three in the eighth, with Elly De La Cruz driving in the winning run with a sacrifice fly in the top of the 10th as the Reds snapped a three-game skid with a 5-4 comeback win over the Chicago White Sox. Rhett Lowder and Luis Castillo, meanwhile, are basically statistical twins right now — "struggling mid-rotation arms producing nearly identical contact and run-prevention outcomes" with near-matching ERAs and WHIPs. Castillo, a former Red, gets the nod for pNERD (5.21) thanks to solid velocity and strike-throwing, though his 29-run "luck" figure suggests his results should actually get worse, not better. Lowder's 3.90 pNERD is unspectacular but respectable for a 24-year-old finding his footing. Team-wise, the White Sox's tNERD (7.82) benefits from a young, affordable roster and a strong bullpen, while Cincinnati's dreadful batting runs drag its tNERD down to 5.13 despite a healthy barrel rate. The 11.03 gNERD lands right around today's average — not a must-watch, but not a total pass either, especially if the offense-friendly humidity forecast holds up.

Milwaukee Brewers @ San Diego Padres, 6:40p

Summary

This one's a genuine top-shelf watch: both teams and both bullpens are elite by NERD's measure, and Kyle Harrison is dealing. Unfortunately, our web searches turned up nothing specific and concrete on current storylines for this particular matchup, so the case here rests almost entirely on the underlying numbers—and those numbers are loud.

Harrison's 11.28 pNERD is comfortably above the 95th percentile historically, built on a 69.0 xFIP- mark that suggests real swing-and-miss stuff, backed by a quick pace and youth on his side. Buehler is the modest half of this pairing, scuffling by peripherals (his 101 xFIP- is dead league-average) but running a lucky +25 mark that's propping up results better than his stuff deserves—expect some correction toward mediocrity. Both lineups grade out virtually identically at tNERD readings near 9.6, among the best team scores you'll see in this dataset, thanks largely to bullpens that both rank near the top of the league in run prevention. Add San Diego's well-regarded broadcast booth, and this lands as one of today's best options and one of the better games you'll find on any given night.

Pittsburgh Pirates @ Miami Marlins, 3:40p

Summary

Two aces with real velocity meeting in a dome that eats offense—this one's worth clearing your evening for, though the "ace" tag comes with an asterisk this season. The Rockies, mired in a lost season at 46-73, got run out of Chase Field 9-0 the night before, with Nolan Arenado hitting a grand slam off his former club — his 18th homer of the year — and the D-backs' bullpen barely breaking a sweat. That result colors the watchability here more than any NERD number does: Arizona's tNERD (4.51) edges Colorado's (1.39) thanks to solid baserunning and fielding, but neither offense is doing much of note, and both club's overall gNERD of 2.37 sits near the bottom of both the historic and today's ranges. The pitching matchup doesn't help. Sugano, in just his second MLB season after a long, decorated run in Japan, was a back-end starter for Baltimore last year before joining Colorado, and his xFIP-driven components are all negative. Mitch Bratt, a 22-year-old lefty who beat out Kohl Drake for the final rotation spot as Soroka made his way back, has flashed some promise — allowing just 1 run in 12 innings against Cleveland and San Diego — but his shaky command numbers still leave him with the lowest pNERD in the pool. Unless you're deeply invested in Chase Field sightlines, this one's skippable.

Detail

Milwaukee Brewers @ San Diego Padres, 6:40p

Summary

I have plenty for a solid draft.

Milwaukee's best-in-baseball roster rolls into Petco Park behind one of the game's quietest aces, and this one has the numbers to back up the hype. At 17.29, the gNERD score sits well above today's average and near the top of the historical distribution, driven by two above-average lineups and a legitimately compelling pitching matchup. Henderson pairs a 9.85 pNERD with a 2.70 ERA, making his 11th appearance of the 2026 season, lights out for the Brewers since re-joining the rotation in July. His command profile is the real story — a 54.5% zone rate, 69.4% first-pitch-strike rate and 5.2% walk rate back up strong strikeout and swinging-strike marks, and the underlying xFIP suggests this isn't fluky run prevention. Mize, meanwhile, is still finding his footing in San Diego after struggling in his first outing as a Padre against the Arizona Diamondbacks, allowing nine hits and eight runs in just 3.1 innings — his 5.36 pNERD is respectable but he's clearly the lesser arm here. Both bullpens rank near the league's best by runs saved, and San Diego's broadcast ratings and Milwaukee's baserunning give this game extra juice on both sides of the ball. A legitimately great watch.

Tarik Skubal's Dodger Stadium debut is the headline here, and the numbers back up the hype. The reigning ace of the pitching staff, now wearing Dodger blue, makes his first Dodger Stadium start since joining the Dodgers, after allowing two runs in six innings last Tuesday in a tough-luck loss at Wrigley Field in his debut with the team. His 12.04 pNERD is comfortably above today's average and sits in rare territory historically, driven by elite whiff rates, a blistering fastball, and an xFIP- that suggests he's been every bit as good as his shiny ERA implies. Noah Cameron isn't just a sacrificial lamb, though — he's quietly been Kansas City's best story lately, having thrown 23 innings over his past three outings, including eight innings of two-hit, one-run baseball with nine strikeouts, and seven no-hit innings before that. The Dodgers' lineup and bullpen (both well above average) give LA a clear team-level edge, while Kansas City's bullpen has been a genuine liability. With a gNERD of 14.63, this ranks near the top of both today's slate and the broader historical range, making it one of the more watchable matchups on the board.

Philadelphia Phillies @ St. Louis Cardinals, 4:45p

Summary

I'll proceed with the information gathered and write the summary now.

Andrew Painter's return from the wilderness is the real draw here, even if the results haven't caught up to the stuff yet. The Phillies' former top prospect, who blew out his elbow in 2023, finally debuted this spring, but a rocky 14-start stretch got him a 7.06 ERA and a 1-8 record, with the last of those outings a two-inning, six-run disaster against Miami that got him optioned down. He's since been retooling his command in the minors—locating in the zone and cutting down walks was the top priority—and his stuff was never the problem; his pNERD of 6.22 leans heavily on premium velocity (96.2 mph) and youth, with some bad luck actually working in his favor after some tough results. Hunter Dobbins counters for St. Louis with a tidy 5.57 pNERD built on quick pace and a solidly below-average xFIP-, quietly effective if unspectacular. Team-wise, both clubs are middling on offense but the Phillies bring an elite bullpen and baserunning edge, while the Cardinals' extreme youth and payroll thrift juice their tNERD. At 11.55, this gNERD sits a bit above the historical median—not a marquee slate-topper, but Painter's stuff-versus-command drama makes it worth a look.

Detail

Minnesota Twins @ Milwaukee Brewers, 11:10a

Summary

Jacob Misiorowski is must-watch, and even a highly imbalanced pitching matchup can't drag this one below elite territory for a Sunday getaway game. The Brewers' rookie phenom brings a video-game stat line into this one — he's leading the league in ERA, FIP, strikeouts, WHIP, and K/BB ratio, and sits at 11-5 with a 1.63 ERA with his sights on potentially crossing the 200-strikeout threshold. His pNERD of 15.96 is essentially off the charts — miles above today's average of 5.36 and even above the historic 95th percentile — built on absurd swinging-strike and xFIP- numbers paired with a fastball touching triple digits. Across the diamond, Wisconsin native Connor Prielipp is having a solid rookie year overall (6.37 pNERD, above average) but has scuffled lately, allowing three runs in five-plus innings against Seattle most recently. Milwaukee's tNERD of 9.85 is near the top of the league, fueled by strong baserunning and one of the best bullpens around, while Minnesota's offense limps in without Byron Buxton, who's on the injured list since late July with a right hip impingement. With a gNERD of 17.43 — comfortably above today's slate and among the best games recently — this is the one to prioritize if you just want to watch someone make big-league hitters look silly.

Colorado Rockies @ St. Louis Cardinals, 11:15a

Summary

Two last-place-adjacent teams closing out a forgettable series, and the NERD math agrees this one's a skip unless you're desperate for baseball. Colorado sits in the NL West basement and St. Louis isn't much better off, and the pitching matchup does little to change that verdict. Michael Lorenzen will start on Sunday for the Rockies, who had lost four games in a row before McCarthy's monster game, and Lorenzen has a 13.50 ERA in his past three starts. That ugly run shows up in his modest 2.43 pNERD, propped up mostly by tough luck rather than actual dominance—his swinging-strike and strike rates are both well below average. Cardinals starter Michael McGreevy fares a bit better at 3.64 pNERD, helped by his youth (age 25), though his stuff isn't missing many bats either. The Rockies' offense has quietly been productive—Jake McCarthy homered twice in a four-hit night Saturday, giving Colorado the lead with a 420-foot drive and adding his 13th of the season—but that punch is buried under the sport's worst pitching staff. St. Louis's tNERD (5.47) clears Colorado's dismal 1.29 mostly on the strength of a young, cheap roster, but with today's slate averaging 10.96 gNERD, this 6.42 lands firmly in "watch something else" territory.

Detail

Atlanta Braves @ New York Yankees, 12:05p

Summary

Chris Sale on extra rest against a Yankees offense that can't buy a hit right now—this is as good as pitching matchups get on a Saturday. The gNERD score of 15.32 sits near the top of the historical range and above today's average, and it's easy to see why: Sale, fresh off National League Pitcher of the Month honors in July, carries a 9.47 pNERD thanks to elite xFIP-, sharp swinging-strike numbers, and velocity that at age 37 is somehow still climbing, with his manager crediting extra rest between starts. "(Extra rest) is one of the things that has kept him strong and kept his velocity where it's at," Braves manager Walt Weiss said, "It's crazy to think about, but at 37 years old, he's producing some of the highest velocities of his career. Cole brings a respectable 6.75 pNERD, with mid-90s heat and strong strike-throwing, though his sinker has been a genuine liability and the Yankees' offense has been ice-cold for weeks, setting up a strength-on-weakness clash against Atlanta's power bats. The Braves also arrive having just seen their season-high eight-game winning streak end when Atlanta blew a save, with Austin Riley and Matt Olson both going deep in that loss. Both tNERDs sit comfortably above average, with the Yankees' barrel rate and baserunning giving them a slight edge. This is a marquee pitching duel worth clearing your schedule for.

Summary

A dominant young arm chasing history against a shorthanded but scrappy Nationals lineup makes this one of the day's best watches. Chase Burns brings a 13-1 record and a shot at becoming the first Reds pitcher in 70 years to notch 13 straight winning decisions, and his 9.87 pNERD backs it up — a mid-90s heater, elite whiff rate, and xFIP- in the mid-80s make him one of the more electric arms you'll see this month, historically top-quartile. Washington counters with lefty Andrew Alvarez, whose respectable-but-unspectacular 5.66 pNERD (that walk rate is a bit shaky) won't scare anyone, though Washington's lineup — paced by Luis García Jr. and missing James Wood to the IL — still ranks as one of the game's top offenses by tNERD (9.31), thanks largely to strong batting runs and baserunning value. The Reds, fresh off dropping the series opener 5-3 and now without Hunter Greene (elbow surgery), lean almost entirely on Burns to save the day. Both bullpens are shaky, so if Burns tires early, expect fireworks late. Overall gNERD of 15.19 sits near the top of today's slate and comfortably above the historical average.

Both offenses are unremarkable — Detroit's barrel rate is a bright spot, San Francisco's is a genuine weakness — and both bullpens are below average. At 10.22, the gNERD lands almost exactly on the historical average and below today's slate average, so this is a game to watch for Jobe's return story, not for star power up and down the lineup.

Cleveland Guardians @ Chicago White Sox, 4:40p

Summary

Cleveland's on a three-game losing streak and just got run out of town by the Mets, while Chicago is nursing bruises from a four-hour, 13-inning heartbreaker against Boston — so this AL Central tilt has a "please just get through this weekend" energy that oddly makes it more watchable, not less. The headline is the rookie lefty duel: Noah Schultz is slated to start for the White Sox against fellow left-hander Parker Messick in a duel of rookies. Messick has been the real deal, backed by strong strikeout and command marks that drive his 7.68 pNERD, and his tidy xFIP- makes him one of the more efficient young arms around. Schultz, still just 22, throws hard at 95-plus but has been homer-prone and wild in the zone, with an xFIP- that lags his shiny recent outing — his negative luck value hints some correction toward better results is plausible. Both rosters skew young and cheap, which the tNERD payroll and age components reward, pushing Chicago's team score toward the top of today's range. At 13.53, this game's gNERD sits comfortably above both the historic and today's averages — worth carving out time for.

Washington's tNERD of 9.27 is built on real thump: they're posting strong batting and baserunning numbers with a roster that averages just 27.1 years old, though their bullpen (-27.8 runs) is a five-alarm fire waiting to undo any lead. Cincinnati, fresh off completing a sweep of Oakland behind Andrew Abbott's sixth win, brings a middling 5.21 tNERD, dragged down by poor batting runs and its own shaky relief corps. On the mound, Cade Cavalli—still building back after Tommy John recovery—sits at 8-5 with 133 strikeouts and a tidy 81 xFIP-, backed by a 96.6 mph fastball that grades out well above average, worth his 7.00 pNERD. Minnesota Twins @ Milwaukee Brewers, 4:40p

Summary

Milwaukee's bullpen is red-hot and Minnesota's defense is a mess, which pretty much tells you everything about why this game leans watchable despite two names casual fans won't recognize. The Brewers own the NL's best record and are riding a three-game home winning streak, with a tNERD of 9.44 fueled by strong baserunning, a deep bullpen, and a young, cost-effective roster. Minnesota, by contrast, is a middling road team with negative marks in fielding and baserunning, dragging their tNERD down to 2.61. On the mound, Shane Drohan gets the spotlight: since debuting this April, he's been the superior arm here, and he has reliably pitched six innings the last month or so, posting a 3.48 ERA and 3.02 FIP with 89 strikeouts this season, and this is his first career appearance against Minnesota. Zebby Matthews, freshly recalled from Triple-A after Joe Ryan's IL stint, brings positive pNERD largely from good luck and velocity rather than dominant peripherals — betting markets and prop analysts favor Drohan's cleaner strikeout profile. Boston's rookie ace is quietly building a resume worth tuning in for, while the Athletics roll out a struggling arm on the tail end of a brutal skid — this one's lopsided but has a legitimate pitching story worth watching. Payton Tolle, the 23-year-old lefty, has been a revelation: he's posting a 3.297 ERA, 1.1485 WHIP, and 9.8 K/9 over 101 innings, backed by a four-seam fastball that sits at 96.1 mph with a 25.0% whiff rate and a curveball generating a 45.7% whiff rate. San Francisco's starter is still unannounced, so that half of the marquee is a total mystery with zero data to judge. Both offenses carry modest tNERD marks in the mid-4s, right around league average, with Detroit's fielding and Giants' bullpen and baserunning dragging things down further. At a gNERD of 9.04, this one lands below both the historical average and today's slate average—background noise rather than appointment viewing.

The tNERD gap (0.90 vs. 5.41) reflects the Rockies' historically bad season, and with a gNERD of 6.78—below both today's slate average and the long-run historical median—this one's easy to skip unless you're a Cardinals completionist.

Detail

Pittsburgh Pirates @ Milwaukee Brewers, 4:40p

Summary

The Brewers are running away with the NL Central and now get to face a Cy Young winner who's quietly been scuffling — this one's got both star power and a legitimate "can Skenes fix himself" storyline. Paul Skenes carries a gaudy 156 strikeouts and 1.11 WHIP into the start, but he's been rocked for a combined 10 runs in 9 1/3 innings in his past two starts, ballooning his ERA to 3.90 — a rare rough patch for a pitcher whose underlying stuff (upper-90s velocity, elite whiff rate) still grades out as one of the best in baseball, evidenced by his 10.98 pNERD. Opposite him, Kyle Harrison makes his first start since landing on the IL with forearm tightness back on July 11, adding some rust-shaking intrigue to an already loaded pitching matchup — his 10.63 pNERD is nearly identical to Skenes'. Milwaukee, at 9.25 tNERD, brings the best record in baseball, plus strong baserunning and a bullpen that grades out as one of the league's better units. Add it up and you get an 18.92 gNERD, comfortably above both the historical 95th percentile (14.76) and today's slate average — this is the game to watch.

Miami Marlins @ Atlanta Braves, 4:15p

Summary

Good under-the-radar arm show tucked into a division race, with Eury Pérez's triple-digit heat pushing the day's top pitcher NERD in this matchup. Atlanta enters on a roll, having taken game one of this series 4-2 behind Ozzie Albies and Austin Riley homers, and now looking to extend their winning streak to a season-high seven games against a Miami club that's road-weary and shorthanded. Pérez brings a 98.2 mph average heater and a strikeout-heavy profile that anchors his 7.62 pNERD, the better of the two starters today, while Grant Holmes carrying six scoreless innings before Austin Riley's two-run shot sealed it in Tuesday's opener shows Atlanta's rotation depth even without Chris Sale and an injured Reynaldo López. Elder counters with a serviceable 4.94 pNERD, buoyed by a quick pace but dinged by middling swing-and-miss stuff; still, since the All-Star break Elder has made three starts, going 2-0 with a 2.12 ERA, and in his most recent outing threw six strong innings against Washington. Miami's tNERD (9.61) is the story on the offensive side — young, cheap, and running well — but that's offset by a bullpen that's a wreck, with four key relievers all on the injured list, which could turn a tight pitchers' duel into a late-inning track meet. With a 14.27 gNERD, this sits comfortably above both the historic and today's averages, making it one of the more watchable matchups on the board.

Summary

Boston is baseball's hottest team right now, and this White Sox-Red Sox matchup gives it a real pitching duel to go with the offense. The Red Sox have won 24 of their last 27 games, riding a five-game winning streak over Chicago into this one, including a 14-2 win Tuesday featuring a season-high four home runs, Caleb Durbin's first career grand slam, and a pair of homers from Wilyer Abreu. That's a tough act to follow, but the pitching matchup looks better than the box score suggests: Sean Burke owns the higher pNERD here, backed by strong strikeout stuff and a favorable xFIP-, while Sonny Gray brings similarly stingy xFIP- numbers despite diminished velocity and a plodding pace that dings his score. Gray has history with Chicago too — he's 7-2 with a 3.26 ERA in 14 career games against the White Sox, though he hasn't faced them since 2024. Detail

Pittsburgh Pirates @ Milwaukee Brewers, 4:40p

Summary

The Brewers own a massive division lead but the Pirates have quietly been their kryptonite lately, and this game pairs two of the more electric young arms in the league. Jared Jones just came back from a two-month injured-list stint and has rediscovered his stuff in July, posting a 2.00 ERA over five starts, and his velocity (98.5 mph average, a huge z-score outlier) and elite xFIP- back it up—hence a hearty 9.82 pNERD. Across from him, Logan Henderson has been arguably better on the ledger sheet, running a minuscule 70 xFIP- with a strong strikeout rate that lands him at 9.78 pNERD, continuing an 8-1 career run that includes a scoreless outing against the Giants his last time out. On the team side, Milwaukee's 9.17 tNERD is buoyed by a deep, young roster with strong baserunning and bullpen numbers, while Pittsburgh's 6.93 isn't far behind thanks to solid batting and baserunning of their own—fitting, given they've won four straight against the Brewers, including Monday's 4-3 series-opening upset. Add it up and you get a 17.85 gNERD, comfortably above both the historical and today's averages—this one's worth your evening.

Los Angeles Dodgers @ Chicago Cubs, 5:05p

Summary

Skubal traded to the Dodgers, making his debut against a lineup that isn't even his old team — that's the headline here, and it's a legitimately fun watch. This is Tarik Skubal's first start as a Dodger, coming to Wrigley just days after L.A. sent a package to Detroit to get him, and his 12.51 pNERD says the hype is earned. His shiny surface stats undersell it: Skubal carries a 31.0% strikeout rate with just a 3.7% walk rate this season, and his 0.910 WHIP ranks among the best in baseball, and his swinging-strike and strike-rate z-scores are near the top of the league, backed by a stingy xFIP-. He's also been on a run before the trade — in his past six outings, Skubal has given up only eight earned runs in 37 innings for an ERA of 1.95 — so this isn't just name value. Assad is a solid, unspectacular caretaker in the back half of the rotation with a low swinging-strike rate that drags his pNERD to a modest 2.75, and the Cubs are missing several top arms this series, which only widens the pitching gap. Both offenses carry real thump, though: the Dodgers' bat-heavy, deep lineup and a Cubs defense with an outstanding fielding number both push their tNERDs near 9.3, among the best pairings you'll see today or in the wider dataset, and Wrigley Field adds ambiance to a gNERD score (16.90) that ranks near the top of the pack.

This series opener slugfest sequel has real upside: the Yankees are chasing a bounce-back after Monday's wild 13-7 loss where Alec Burleson hit three homers off them, and Tuesday brings a legitimately compelling pitching matchup to boot. Ryan Weathers, the Yankees' lefty, owns the better peripherals here — his 79 xFIP- and 8.36 pNERD suggest he's pitching better than his 3.99 ERA lets on, and he's actually been a bit unlucky, so there's more in the tank than the raw numbers show. Hunter Dobbins, back from an ACL tear that ended his Red Sox tenure and now starting for St. Louis after the offseason trade for Willson Contreras, brings a solid 6.00 pNERD and a lively 95-plus mph fastball. New York's lineup is banged up — Aaron Judge (rib), Giancarlo Stanton (leg), and Cody Bellinger (leg) are all out — but the Yankees still post an 8.07 tNERD thanks to elite barrel rates and a deep bullpen, comfortably above both the historic and today's-game averages. Add in a Cardinals offense that just dropped 13 runs on this same pitching staff, and the 13.95 gNERD checks out: this one lands well above the historic median and near the top of today's slate.

Jesús Luzardo brings swing-and-miss stuff and a Nationals lineup that's mashing everything not named Luzardo, making this the rare Nats-Phillies game worth clearing your schedule for. Luzardo carries a strikeout rate near 29% and a tidy 3.57 ERA into the outing, though he's looking to bounce back from allowing six runs in 6.1 innings to the Marlins last time out, after allowing just eight earned runs in 49.1 innings across his previous eight starts. His pNERD of 10.58 backs that up — well above the 95th percentile for today's games — thanks to a strong xFIP-, plush velocity, and a bit of positive regression coming his way. Littell, by contrast, is scuffling for a Washington rotation gutted by injuries; the Nationals have DJ Herz, Josiah Gray, Mitchell Parker, Ken Waldichuk, and Connelly Early all on the injured list, leaving the club relying heavily on Littell despite his 5.94 FIP and negative WAR. That mismatch drags the pitching side down, but Washington's offense — young, athletic, and running wild on the bases — pushes the Nationals' tNERD to 9.24, comfortably above the historic 95th percentile. Philadelphia's bullpen depth and broadcast ratings add just enough polish to make the 13.19 gNERD a solidly above-average watch.

Miami's low-payroll, high-baserunning Marlins bring some genuine juice into Truist Park, even if Vegas thinks this is a laugher waiting to happen. The Braves are the far bigger name here, but the Marlins actually carry the better tNERD (9.82 to 6.31), fueled by a recovery from a franchise-record 12-game losing streak to win six of seven, including three straight against the New York Mets, plus a young, cheap roster that's been running better than its underlying luck number suggests. Atlanta counters with its own hot streak — riding a five-game winning streak after going 12-5 since the All-Star break, including a four-game weekend sweep over the Washington Nationals — but its tNERD gets docked for negative batted-luck and an older, pricier roster that doesn't get bonus points here. On the mound, Ryan Gusto (pNERD 5.12) is scuffling on the surface — 0-2 with a 5.31 ERA and 1.44 WHIP — but his underlying numbers and tough luck number suggest better days ahead. Grant Holmes (pNERD 2.99) is the steadier stat-line arm at 6-4, 3.88 ERA, 1.36 WHIP, though he gave up a season-high three home runs in his last outing against the Nationals. The 12.13 gNERD lands a bit above the historical average, mostly on the strength of Miami's team profile rather than a marquee pitching duel.

A former Twins washout is quietly outdueling his old team's ace, and that oddity alone makes this worth a glance — even if the underlying NERD math says skip it. Kansas City's Randy Dobnak, who was designated for assignment and bounced to the Mariners before Kansas City picked him up, has been the story of this series: Dobnak, the longtime Twin who was acquired by Kansas City from Seattle in June, has been outstanding since his debut with the Royals on July 2. Just last Wednesday he tossed seven shutout innings against his former club, permitting four hits and one walk in seven innings while striking out four, matching a career high and marking the first time he'd thrown more than 100 pitches in a start. Joe Ryan, meanwhile, is scuffling — he's 1-4 with a 4.91 ERA over his last six starts, allowing 12 runs and 18 hits in 10 innings of the past two — though his xFIP- of 87 still says he's the better bet on paper, and he owns this game's only pitcher NERD score of note (6.23) thanks to strong strike-throwing and whiff rates. Dobnak's pNERD (3.14) is a mirage built on a tidy ERA rather than real stuff. Team-wise, both clubs are duds: Minnesota's bullpen and defense are dragging its tNERD to 2.73, and Kansas City's bullpen (-36.5 runs) is arguably the worst in the league, propping up its 3.01 mark only via positive luck. Los Angeles Dodgers @ Chicago Cubs, 5:05p

Summary

This one has real juice: two 60-plus-win rivals, elite defenses, and a Cubs offense trying to snap out of a funk against a Dodgers club nursing a bruised ego after getting swept by Boston. The gNERD of 14.45 sits well above both the historical average (10.11) and today's slate (10.80), driven almost entirely by two outstanding team profiles — Dodgers (9.41) and Cubs (9.31) both rank near the top of the historic tNERD distribution, fueled by strong batting runs and, in the Cubs' case, an absurd fielding-runs mark of 55.6. The Dodgers arrive looking to reset after Dave Roberts admitted "They outplayed us" in a series where Boston outscored Los Angeles 20-10 over the three games, costing them the best record in baseball. Matthew Boyd (5.19 pNERD, solid strike-throwing and respectable xFIP-) takes the mound for Chicago, while the Dodgers' listed TBD starter is actually expected to be Justin Wrobleski, who enters with a 2.88 ERA over 112.2 IP despite peripherals suggesting he's been pretty lucky this year. Add in a Cubs bullpen that's shaky and a Dodgers pen anchored by a bounced-back Tanner Scott, and this is a legitimately watchable ballgame.

St. Louis Cardinals @ New York Yankees, 4:05p

Summary

Cam Schlittler's electric arm makes this one worth catching, even if the Cardinals side of the ledger looks bleak. This is Schlittler's Cy Young-caliber season on display — the right-hander carries a 2.04 ERA and has struck out 165 batters this season, backed by a blistering four-seam fastball that sits at 97.9 mph and generates a 30.4% whiff rate with a .234 xwOBA against. His pNERD of 10.54 is comfortably above today's average and sits near the top of the historical distribution, fueled by elite strikeout stuff and top-shelf velocity. McGreevy, by contrast, is scuffling badly — his last outing saw him come against the Cubs on July 28, one of the roughest starts of his season, lasting only 1⅔ innings while allowing seven earned runs — and his 3.67 pNERD reflects thin whiff and strike-rate numbers. The Yankees' 8.16 tNERD, boosted by strong barrel rate and baserunning marks, dwarfs a punchless Cardinals lineup dealing with a slump; St. Louis has fallen under .500 with seven losses in their last 10 games and sits four games out of the final wild card spot. New York is banged up too, with Aaron Judge, Cody Bellinger, and Carlos Rodón all on the injured list, but that hardly dents this gNERD of 13.82, which lands well above both the historical and today's averages — mostly on the strength of one dominant arm.

Detail

Milwaukee Brewers @ Los Angeles Angels, 12:15p

Summary

This is the day's marquee pitching matchup, and it's not particularly close. Jacob Misiorowski takes the mound fresh off a start where he struck out the first seven Rockies batters to set a Brewers franchise record, then retired the first 14 hitters he faced before a two-out homer in the fifth, and he's doing it while setting a pitch-tracking-era record by throwing all 66 of his fastballs at least 100 mph. His 15.66 pNERD is comfortably the best of any pitcher in today's slate, built on elite whiff rates, a sub-50 xFIP-, and velocity that sits near the top of the league — this is a legitimate NL Cy Young caliber arm. Walbert Ureña isn't chopped liver either, pairing a mid-90s-plus fastball with a 6.46 pNERD, though he leans on that heater more than most (over half his pitches) and his strikeout rate looks a bit lucky. On the team side, Milwaukee's 9.42 tNERD (young, athletic, good bullpen) dwarfs a last-place Angels club (1.19 tNERD) currently on a five-game skid with the majors' worst record. Historically this game's 16.37 gNERD ranks near the top of the distribution — well above today's 11.26 average — making it the pick of the day almost entirely on Misiorowski's arm.
